clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, Federal Register of March 3, 1986; held government printing) revokes the orders listed in its table, and any amendments thereto; its enacting provision has no stated effective date, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading, disclosed for the reviewer). The Federal Register publication and filing dates are not effective dates. The table lists 12186, whose subject line describes changing the definition of heavy oil. The single instruction amends Executive Order 12153 by deleting section 1-102, renumbering section 1-103 as 1-102, and replacing the figure 16.0 degrees API with 20.0 degrees API in section 1-101. Executive Order 12189 of January 16, 1980 later amended Executive Order 12153, as amended by this order, to read as follows (before: this order’s single 20.0 degrees API definition; after: separate definitions for August 17 to December 20, 1979 and for December 21, 1979 and thereafter, with the section numbering restated). That is a strike-and-insert rewrite under owner ruling 2026-10-21: the clause continues, amended, and the substance of the definition changed. Whether the authority of the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973 lapsed before 1986 is not established from held sources (the statute text is not held), and such a lapse would be an unnamed instrument and a disclosed candidate only. Executive Order 12287 of January 28, 1981 (held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12287.txt; not among this packet’s citable evidence) exempted all crude oil and refined petroleum products from the price and allocation controls adopted under that Act without naming this order; it is likewise a disclosed candidate earlier end and not an end, and it is not recorded as a later event. No earlier express end was found.
